reason: E2 directly supports the structural stability up to 96 GPa and the continuous Tc increase, and explicitly contrasts this with Nb and Ta, supporting the first three premises. However, the mechanistic link between structural stability and Tc behavior (premise 4) and the role of configurational entropy in averaging the electronic structure (premise 5) are not directly evidenced in the cited passages; they are inferred rather than supported by specific prior evidence.
premises: The bcc structure of (TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33 is stable up to ~96 GPa without phase transition.
Tc of this HEA increases continuously up to 96 GPa under pressure.
The pressure dependence of Tc in this HEA is distinct from that of elemental Nb and Ta.
The robust bcc structure under pressure is linked to the unusual Tc behavior.
High configurational entropy leads to a chemically averaged electronic structure that maintains electron–phonon coupling.
